newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 24.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
* China now draws more than one-third of all investment in factories and other manufacturing operations in developing nations, according to a World Bank study.
* Smokers will probably not benefit much from a companion plan Liggett Group announced last week to settle all present and future suits by smokers, their survivors, cities, counties and insurers.
* News Analysis: If a labour dispute at AMR's American Airlines is settled in favor of certain pilot demands, it could have broad industry labour implications.
* Advanced Micro Devices chief executive W.J. Sanders 3rd got a small salary increase last year but received stock options with a current value exceeding $60 million.
* The U.S. Supreme Court must decide where to place the Internet under the First Amendment before determining how much protection to give it.
* Nike has added advertising firm Goodby, Silverstein & Partners to its list and dismissed the Leap Partnership and Gateway 2000 hired D'Arcy Masius Benton & Bowles.
* Jessie Lee Brown Foveaux, who wrote her memoirs at age 80, is an example of how commercial success in publishing can hinge on news attention.
* Some Internet companies are rethinking the unlimited $19.95 per month service plan.
* While "push technology" has received lots of attention as a way to find information on the Internet, the browser is not dead yet.
* The Web's official Oscar site is one of the best places on the Internet to find information about the Academy Awards.
* A shake-up at advertising agency Leo Burnett was the result of growing internal frustrations at the firm.
* Philanthropy magazines are a new way to tap a market of high net-worth households.
* San Diego is becoming known as the Wireless Valley, a center for the telecommunications industry.
